title: Rework presubmit profiles and introduce dependency-categorizer tool
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Consolidates presubmit lanes, adds a dependency categorizer CLI, and introduces a CI gate to warn/fail on unclassified devdeps. No runtime changes.
description:
Context: Over time our presubmit matrix has proliferated (lint-*, test-*, e2e-*, smoke-nightly) which increases CI flakiness and developer cognitive load. Separately, dependency churn in package.json/requirements.txt has led to accidental promotion of dev-only packages into build/runtime surfaces. This PR accomplishes three goals in one cohesive change: 1) Rework presubmit profiles to a smaller set of intent-driven lanes (quicklint, unit-fastpath, integration-stable) with clear signal vs cost tradeoffs; 2) Introduce a new CLI tool (tools/dep-categorizer) that scans JS/Python manifests and suggests classification tags (prod/dev/optional/tooling) using heuristics augmented by a small whitelist/blacklist; 3) Add a lightweight CI gate that surfaces unclassified/uncategorized dependencies and optionally fails the presubmit when the unclassified delta exceeds a small threshold. Description of changes: - Presubmit refactor: replaced four specialized lint/test workflows with three lanes. Mapped existing jobs into lanes using path-aware selectors and added concise annotations to each job so humans can reason about cost. - dep-categorizer: new Go-based CLI that reads package.json/pyproject.toml/requirements.txt and emits a JSON summary and a suggested patch (works with --apply to create a dep-classification.yml entry). The heuristics prefer filepaths, import usage scan, and an internal whitelist for known infra libs. - CI gate: a new lightweight GH Action that runs dep-categorizer and uploads a summarized comment to the PR; the action exits non-zero only if the number of new unclassified deps > 3 or if an allowlist is not present for changes touching infra/installer. - Migration: existing branch protection and CODEOWNERS remain unchanged. Team leads (infra, sdk, docs) received migration notes and an automated label mapping to preserve behavior for jobs that had repo-specific skips. Why this is safe: changes are CI and dev tooling only; no production runtime paths modified. The dep-categorizer can run in dry-run mode; the gate is opt-in via label 'ci-enforce-dep-classification' (we enabled it repo-wide for a one-week ramp after merge). Checklist:
- [x] Presubmit lanes validated on a replica repo with the new mapping
- [x] dep-categorizer unit tests and small corpus run against redwood/ and redwood-sdk-python/
- [x] Added integration test for the GH Action to simulate an unclassified dep delta
- [x] Documentation: docs/dev/ci-presubmit.md and docs/dev/dependency-guidelines.md updated
Notes for reviewers: focus on the lane mappings in .github/workflows/presubmit-matrix.yml and on the dep-categorizer heuristics (tools/dep-categorizer/heuristics.go). The CLI is intentionally conservative; please pay attention to the classification whitelist and the opt-in enforcement mechanism.

review_comments: Ethan Park (2026-02-19): Thanks — high level I'm supportive. Two asks: (1) please add a toggle to keep the old matrix for one week (we need a rollback path for releases), and (2) can dep-categorizer emit a deterministic fingerprint so CI comments are stable?

Priya Shah (2026-02-19): @Ethan good catches — added a repo-wide temporary toggle (GITHUB_ENV PRESUBMIT_LEGACY=1) and a fingerprint field (sha256 of sorted dep list) to the JSON output. Updated commits reflect those changes.
Marceline Du (2026-02-20): The heuristics.go looks fine but the Python import scanner is expensive. Can we sample only changed files rather than the whole repo by default?
Priya Shah (2026-02-20): Updated heuristics to prefer import scanning of changed files (falls back to full scan with --force). Added tests to verify sampling behavior.
Riley Nguyen (2026-02-21): CI Action had one flaky run because of transient network to the dependency registry. Can we cache registry metadata for 1h?
Priya Shah (2026-02-21): Added short-lived cache for registry metadata and a retry loop with exponential backoff. Reran CI.
Ethan Park (2026-02-22): Approved after the cache/retry tweaks. Left a minor nit about comment language in the GH Action (suggested wording change).
Marceline Du (2026-02-22): Approved. Requested follow-up to add a daily job that runs dep-categorizer across all repos and populates a central index (ENG-7450).
Riley Nguyen (2026-02-22): Approved. Verified that the presubmit lanes reduce median feedback time in a smoke run.
